# Elasticsearch MCP connector

Let your AI explore and query your Elasticsearch cluster on Elastic Cloud, Serverless or your own servers: list indices and data streams, read mappings, search, aggregate, count, run ES|QL and, with … The AnythingMCP connector gives Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and Gemini 16 MCP tools for Elasticsearch: 12 read and 4 can change data.

## Start without code

No installation and no terminal: AnythingMCP Cloud runs the Elasticsearch connector for you, operated by helpcode.ai in Frankfurt, Germany.

1. **Click the button above** and create an account or sign in. The Elasticsearch connector opens, ready to install.
2. **Paste the API key or token from your Elasticsearch account.** Every click is in the [step-by-step guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/elasticsearch-to-mcp).
3. **Click Install.** AnythingMCP shows the address of your MCP server.
4. **Add that address to your assistant:** [Claude](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-claude) · [ChatGPT](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-chatgpt) · [Microsoft Copilot](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-copilot) · [Cursor](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-cursor) · [Gemini CLI](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-gemini) · [Meta Muse](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-elasticsearch-to-muse).
5. **Ask your first question**, for example: *Show invoice INV-2026-045 in invoices-2026 and confirm amount, due date and payment status.*

Prefer help with the setup? [Talk to us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["Claude · ChatGPT · Copilot · Cursor"]
  amcp["AnythingMCP<br/>roles · audit log · encrypted credentials"]
  api["Elasticsearch API"]
  client -- "MCP, OAuth or API key" --> amcp
  amcp -- "HTTPS, an API key" --> api
```

- **The AI client** speaks MCP (Streamable HTTP) to AnythingMCP and only sees tool names, descriptions and results. It never gets the Elasticsearch credentials.
- **AnythingMCP** checks the client's role, builds the call from the tool definition, adds the credentials (an API key), calls Elasticsearch, logs the call and returns the result.
- **Elasticsearch** sees an ordinary API client with the rights of the account the credentials belong to.

## Tool reference

Every parameter as the AI client sees it in `tools/list`. Source: [`packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/elasticsearch.json`](../../../packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/elasticsearch.json).

### `elasticsearch_whoami`

Show who the connector is signed in as: the user behind the API key, the key's name and id and the authentication type. Needs no privileges, so it is the first check when another tool answers 401 or 403. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /_security/_authenticate`

No parameters.

### `elasticsearch_cluster_info`

Get basic information about the cluster: name, uuid, Elasticsearch version and build flavor (serverless on Elastic Cloud Serverless). Needs the monitor cluster privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /`

No parameters.

### `elasticsearch_cluster_health`

Get the cluster health: status (green, yellow or red), node counts, active, relocating, initializing and unassigned shards and pending tasks. Not available on Elastic Cloud Serverless, where Elastic runs the cluster. Needs the monitor cluster privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /_cluster/health/{index}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | no | Limit the health check to these indices or data streams (comma-separated, wildcards allowed). Default * for the whole cluster. |

### `elasticsearch_list_indices`

List indices with their health, status, document count, store size, primary and replica shard counts and creation date, sorted by name (at most 500 rows). Data stream backing indices start with .ds-. Use it to find the index name before searching. Needs the monitor privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /_cat/indices/{index}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | no | Index name or pattern to list, e.g. logs-* or products. Default * (all). |
| `expand_wildcards` | `open` \| `all` \| `closed` \| `hidden` | no | Which indices a pattern matches: open (default, skips hidden and closed ones) or all. |
| `health` | `green` \| `yellow` \| `red` | no | Only list indices with this health. |

### `elasticsearch_get_mapping`

Get the field mapping of an index or data stream: every field with its type (text, keyword, date, long, dense_vector...). Read it before writing a query so field names and types are right; keyword fields take exact term filters, text fields take match queries. Needs view_index_metadata. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /{index}/_mapping`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Index, data stream or alias to search, e.g. products. Wildcards and comma-separated lists work (logs-*,metrics-*). |

### `elasticsearch_search`

Search an index, data stream or alias with the Query DSL and get the matching documents (total, and per hit _index, _id, _score, _source and highlights). Returns 10 hits by default and never more than 100; page with from or with search_after plus sort. Use source_fields to return only the fields you need. Common vector fields are dropped from the output. Needs the read privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `POST /{index}/_search`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Index, data stream or alias to search, e.g. products. Wildcards and comma-separated lists work (logs-*,metrics-*). |
| `query` | object | no | Query DSL object, the value of the query key, e.g. {"match": {"title": "running shoes"}} or {"bool": {"filter": [{"term": {"status": "active"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d"}}}]}}. Leave it out to match every document. |
| `size` | integer | no | Number of hits to return, 0 to 100 (default 10). |
| `from` | integer | no | Offset of the first hit, for paging (from + size must stay under 10,000). |
| `sort` | any[] | no | Sort order, e.g. [{"@timestamp": "desc"}] or [{"price": {"order": "asc"}}]. Sort on keyword, numeric or date fields, not on text fields. |
| `source_fields` | string[] | no | Only return these fields of each document (wildcards allowed, e.g. ["title", "price", "user.*"]). |
| `highlight` | object | no | Highlight settings, e.g. {"fields": {"description": {}}} to show where the query matched. |
| `search_after` | any[] | no | The sort values of the last hit of the previous page, to fetch the next page (requires sort). |
| `track_total_hits` | boolean | no | true counts every match exactly; by default Elasticsearch stops counting at 10,000 and reports relation gte. |

### `elasticsearch_aggregate`

Run aggregations over an index or data stream without returning documents: counts per value (terms), sums and averages, date histograms, percentiles and more, optionally on a filtered subset. Returns the total match count and the aggregations. Needs the read privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `POST /{index}/_search`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Index, data stream or alias to search, e.g. products. Wildcards and comma-separated lists work (logs-*,metrics-*). |
| `aggs` | object | yes | Aggregations object, e.g. {"by_brand": {"terms": {"field": "brand", "size": 10}}, "avg_price": {"avg": {"field": "price"}}} or {"per_day": {"date_histogram": {"field": "@timestamp", "calendar_interval": "day"}}}. Use keyword, numeric or date fields. |
| `query` | object | no | Query DSL object, the value of the query key, e.g. {"match": {"title": "running shoes"}} or {"bool": {"filter": [{"term": {"status": "active"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d"}}}]}}. Leave it out to match every document. |
| `track_total_hits` | boolean | no | true counts every match exactly instead of stopping at 10,000. |

### `elasticsearch_count`

Count the documents in an index, data stream or alias that match a query (all documents without a query). Cheaper than a search when only the number matters. Needs the read privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `POST /{index}/_count`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Index, data stream or alias to search, e.g. products. Wildcards and comma-separated lists work (logs-*,metrics-*). |
| `query` | object | no | Query DSL object, the value of the query key, e.g. {"match": {"title": "running shoes"}} or {"bool": {"filter": [{"term": {"status": "active"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d"}}}]}}. Leave it out to match every document. |

### `elasticsearch_esql_query`

Run an ES|QL query (Elasticsearch 8.11 or later, and Serverless), a piped language for filtering, aggregating and joining, e.g. FROM logs-* | WHERE @timestamp > NOW() - 1 day | STATS errors = COUNT(*) BY host.name | SORT errors DESC | LIMIT 20. Returns columns (name, type) and rows as values; at most 500 rows are passed on, so always end with LIMIT. Needs the read privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `POST /_query`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | The ES\|QL query. Start with FROM <index pattern>, end with LIMIT n (Elasticsearch applies LIMIT 1000 when none is given). Use ? placeholders with params for values. |
| `params` | any[] | no | Values for the ? placeholders in order, e.g. ["error", 100], so user input is never pasted into the query text. |
| `filter` | object | no | Optional Query DSL filter applied before the query runs, e.g. {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-1d"}}}. |

### `elasticsearch_get_document`

Get one document by its _id from an index: found, _version and the _source, optionally only some fields. Use the concrete index name (from a search hit's _index), not a pattern. Needs the read privilege. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /{index}/_doc/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | The index that holds the document (a search hit's _index) or an alias pointing to one index. |
| `id` | string | yes | The document _id. |
| `source_includes` | string | no | Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. title,price. Wildcards allowed. |
| `source_excludes` | string | no | Comma-separated fields to leave out, e.g. embedding,raw_html. |

### `elasticsearch_list_aliases`

List index aliases: alias name, the index it points to, whether it has a filter and whether it is the write index. Needs view_index_metadata. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /_cat/aliases/{name}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | Alias name or pattern. Default * (all). |

### `elasticsearch_list_data_streams`

List data streams (time series such as logs and metrics): name, health status, index template, generation, number of backing indices, current write index, lifecycle or ILM policy and timestamp field. Search a data stream by its name like an index. Needs view_index_metadata. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /_data_stream/{name}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | Data stream name or pattern, e.g. logs-*. Default * (all). |

### `elasticsearch_index_document`

Create or replace a whole document under a given _id in an index. Replacing overwrites every field of an existing document. Before calling, show the user the index, the _id and the document and ask them to confirm; never call it without that confirmation. Set op_type create to refuse overwriting an existing document. Needs the write (or index) privilege.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `PUT /{index}/_doc/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Target index or alias (with a write index). |
| `id` | string | yes | The document _id. An existing document with this _id is replaced unless op_type is create. |
| `document` | object | yes | The full document as a JSON object, e.g. {"title": "Red shoe", "price": 79.9}. |
| `op_type` | `index` \| `create` | no | index (default) creates or replaces; create fails with 409 if the _id already exists. |
| `refresh` | `false` \| `wait_for` \| `true` | no | When the change becomes visible to searches: false (default, within about a second), wait_for (the call waits until it is searchable) or true (forces a refresh, avoid on busy indices). |

### `elasticsearch_update_document`

Change some fields of an existing document by _id, leaving the others as they are (a partial update with doc). Before calling, show the user the index, the _id and the fields that will change and ask them to confirm; never call it without that confirmation. Scripts are not supported here. Needs the write (or index) privilege.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /{index}/_update/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | The index that holds the document (a search hit's _index). |
| `id` | string | yes | The document _id. |
| `doc` | object | yes | Only the fields to change, e.g. {"status": "archived"}. Objects are merged, arrays are replaced. |
| `doc_as_upsert` | boolean | no | true creates the document from doc when the _id does not exist yet; by default the update fails with 404. |
| `retry_on_conflict` | integer | no | How often to retry when another write changed the document at the same time (default 0). |
| `refresh` | `false` \| `wait_for` \| `true` | no | When the change becomes visible to searches: false (default, within about a second), wait_for (the call waits until it is searchable) or true (forces a refresh, avoid on busy indices). |

### `elasticsearch_delete_document`

Delete one document by _id. It cannot be undone. Installed switched off; an admin turns it on deliberately. Before calling, show the user the index and the _id and ask them to confirm; never call it without that confirmation. Needs the delete (or write) privilege.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `DELETE /{index}/_doc/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | The index that holds the document (a search hit's _index). |
| `id` | string | yes | The document _id. |
| `refresh` | `false` \| `wait_for` \| `true` | no | When the change becomes visible to searches: false (default, within about a second), wait_for (the call waits until it is searchable) or true (forces a refresh, avoid on busy indices). |

### `elasticsearch_delete_by_query`

Delete every document that matches a query. It cannot be undone and can remove millions of documents. Installed switched off; an admin turns it on deliberately. Before calling, run elasticsearch_count with the same query, tell the user how many documents will be deleted and ask them to confirm; never call it without that confirmation. Needs the delete (or write) privilege.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /{index}/_delete_by_query`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | string | yes | Index, data stream or alias to delete from. Avoid wildcards. |
| `query` | object | yes | Query DSL object selecting the documents to delete, e.g. {"term": {"status": "spam"}}. Required: a match_all here would empty the index. |
| `max_docs` | integer | no | Stop after deleting this many documents. |
| `refresh` | boolean | no | true refreshes the affected shards when done. |

## Run it yourself

AnythingMCP is open source (AGPL-3.0). [Run it with Docker](../../../README.md#run-it-yourself), open **Connectors → Store**, pick **Elasticsearch** and enter `ELASTICSEARCH_URL`, `ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY`, then add your MCP server URL to the AI client.
